I had an experience today, talking w/ a white middle-age male veteran. I'll call him Geoff. He asked me abt my #BlackLivesMatter button -->
I recently had put it on my coat bc I kept forgetting 2 put it on the next day's sweater. Geoff wanted my opinion on #BLM's flag burning -->
"I think if you're going 2wear a #BlackLivesMatter button, u shd be ready 2answer a few questions," he said. He wasn't aggressive abt it -->
I said it was fine; I hadn't realized he was the one saying "Ma'am?" 3 times! "Why does #BLM want to burn the flag? Do u support it?"  -->
"As far as the #BlackLivesMatter group, I can't tell them how they shd deal w/ their grief&rage. This country has let them down..." -->
"But it's complicated, bc u *served* this country&want the flag 2B respected." Geoff adds "I support #BlackLivesMatter bc of ppl I know" -->
"I lived in S Carolina; I know a lot of BP" he went on, "but I don't know if it's right." #BlackLivesMatter -->
I did what I cd 2affirm his uncertainty: "I know; #Itscomplicated &there's no simple answer." He sincerely wanted to *understand*  #BLM -->
We shook hands, exchanged first names. I was so #humbled -- *am* so humbled 2B part of this #BlackLivesMatter movemt & 2B part of @ShowUp4RJ
